theme: Sit at my right hand, the exalted Christ
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 110:1-7. This is the psalm quoted more than any other in the New Testament. Peter uses it on Pentecost to prove that Jesus is exalted at God’s right hand. You first met it in the Old Testament. Read it now as the psalm of the ascension.
settingTheScene: Psalm 110 is a psalm of David about a figure he calls “my Lord.” The psalm describes a king-priest, seated at God’s right hand, who will rule over his enemies. David himself was not a priest, and no king of Israel was both king and priest. Jesus asked the Pharisees how the Christ could be David’s son when David called him Lord (Mark 12:35-37). The answer in Acts is that Jesus, risen and ascended, is the one to whom David spoke.
observation: “The LORD says to my Lord: Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool” (v. 1).
“The LORD sends forth from Zion your mighty scepter. Rule in the midst of your enemies!” (v. 2).
“Your people will offer themselves freely on the day of your power” (v. 3).
“The LORD has sworn and will not change his mind” (v. 4).
“You are a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek” (v. 4).
“The Lord is at your right hand; he will shatter kings on the day of his wrath” (v. 5).
“He will execute judgment among the nations” (v. 6).
“He will drink from the brook by the way; therefore he will lift up his head” (v. 7).
interpretation:
The psalm begins with a conversation in heaven: “The LORD says to my Lord.” The first LORD is Yahweh, and the second is David’s Lord, the Messiah. The Messiah is invited to sit at God’s right hand, the place of honor and authority, until all his enemies are made his footstool. In Acts 2:34-35, Peter says that David did not ascend into the heavens, but he said, “The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand.” Jesus is the Lord to whom David referred. The ascension is the fulfillment of this verse.

The King’s rule extends from Zion. The mighty scepter is sent forth, and he rules in the midst of his enemies. This describes the current age: the King reigns now, though his enemies have not yet been put under his feet. His people willingly offer themselves, “in holy garments,” like an army of volunteers on the day of his power. This describes the church.

Then comes the astonishing oath in verse 4: “You are a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek.” Melchizedek in Genesis 14 was both king of Salem and priest of God Most High, who blessed Abraham. In Israel, kings came from Judah and priests from Levi. This verse promises a priest-king who is outside the Levitical order and whose priesthood is eternal. The book of Hebrews makes this central: Jesus is our great high priest, not by descent from Aaron, but by the oath of God, living forever to intercede for us (Hebrews 5 to 7). The LORD has sworn and will not change his mind. His priesthood is as secure as God’s word.

The last stanza describes the judgment: he will shatter kings on the day of his wrath, execute judgment among the nations, and shatter chiefs over the wide earth. He drinks from the brook by the way and lifts up his head, a picture of a victorious warrior refreshed in the pursuit. The psalm combines the two offices that Acts presents: Jesus as king ruling from heaven and as priest interceding for his people. And the victory is certain.
connection: Genesis 14:18-20 is Melchizedek. Hebrews 1:13, 5:6, 7:1-28, 8:1, and 10:12-13 apply the psalm to Christ. Matthew 22:41-46 records Jesus asking about David’s Lord. Acts 2:34-36 uses verse 1. Ephesians 1:20-22 says God seated Christ at his right hand. 1 Corinthians 15:25 says he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet. Romans 8:34 says Christ is at the right hand of God, interceding for us. Zechariah 6:12-13 describes a priest on his throne.
application:
Remember that Jesus is both king and priest. Bring a need to him as King, and a failure to him as Priest.

Thank him for living forever to intercede for you.

Pray “until I make your enemies your footstool” over a difficult area of the world, and wait for him to act.
prayerPrompts: Worship Jesus at the Father’s right hand.
Thank him for being a priest forever.
Ask him to rule over your enemies, inside and out.
